# The field notes

The reflections written on the walls of the endless museum, in walk order.

Each entry is one line of the book: the sentence a wall hangs, and under it what
was written standing in front of it. The line lives in
`commons/data/book/<chapter>.json` as `text`; the reflection is `note` on the same
line. Both are editable in the museum (click the wall, then the inspector), at
[/wall-map](http://localhost:3003/wall-map), [/wall-texts](http://localhost:3003/wall-texts)
and [/lines](http://localhost:3003/lines).

*Generated by `python tools/field_notes.py --apply`. Do not edit this file — edit
the book, and run it again.*

**20 reflections** across 19 halls in 2 chapters — 3,667 characters, out of 843 lines in the book.

## primitives

### point · `Point_One`

**`origin`**

> *Standing at Vector.ZERO,

Point zero, * ,
Vector(0,0,0)
The root of all vectors.

The origin, No turning back.*

A corner, not a cell. Four cells meet here and none of them contains it, which is why nothing could be centred on the origin until the basin was made even: an odd one has a middle cell, and a corner is not a cell. Three of its four quadrants lie in coordinates no map row can name — the building can stand there, the language cannot. So it was not placed but excavated, two metres down under glass, and became visible by subtraction. While it was being dug, five systems walked into it: a bench, a column, a cornice, a joint, a lit strip. To each of them this was cell (0,0), ordinary floor. It is only the origin because someone says so.

**`CoordinateSystem3M`**

> *Point one, position,
no point without the coordinate system.

3D Space.*

A point is that which has no part, so it has no place either: it borrows its whole existence from a coordinate system that is not itself a point.

### lines · `Point_Lines`

**`klee_walking_point`**

> *A line is a point that went for a walk.*

A line cannot be drawn without two points it did not make, and the instant it measures them it becomes the instrument that makes space addressable.

### trace · `Point_Trace`

**`mystic_writing_pad`**

> *there is no origin of a trace*

The trace is everything the line throws away — duration, hesitation, texture — and it is jagged because a resolution is always already there; it has no origin, only a sampling rate.

### line grid · `Point_Line_Grid`

**`player_trace`**

> *the trace, gridded*

The grid arrives promising neutrality and already owning the ground: every cell is an address, and an address is a claim.

### triangle context · `Point_Triangle_Context`

**`catalyst_pedestal`**

> *the triangle. everything is made of triangles. the quad, the simplest mesh. the pyramid mesh.*

The triangle is the smallest figure that cannot be deformed without breaking, so everything is built from it and nothing built from it can bend.

### polythedra · `Primitives_Polythedra`

**`grab_trihedron`**

> *three faces in the hand*

Five solids and the taxonomy closes; the Platonic set is complete, which is precisely why it cannot hold anything that arrives after it.

### animatedcube · `Point_Animatedcube`

**`animatedcubebuilder`**

> *the cube world, built*

The cube is the first form that fills space rather than describing it, so it eats the world it was meant to measure — and until it is folded it is only a flat net.

### primitives · `Chamber_Primitives`

**`catalyst_target`**

> *primitives — and so on*

The chamber is where the taxonomy stops being looked at and starts looking back, and the boundary between the one who counts and the thing counted is the first primitive to dissolve.

### ignorance · `Primitives_Ignorance`

**`righttriangle`**

> *the right angle is the basis of all rectangular coordinate systems*

The sphere is the question the triangle cannot answer — how many faces — and the answer is a budget, so ignorance here is not missing knowledge but a resolution someone chose.

### portals · `Primitives_Portals`

**`achilles_tortoise`**

> *Achilles and the tortoise: the endlessness of pi in a footrace*

The portal is the edge made walkable: you step through it and arrive at another approach, because pi does not finish and neither does the corridor.

### melencolia · `Primitives_Melencolia`

**`durer_scene`**

> *Dürer's polyhedron — the solid no taxonomy names, and the angel who keeps it*

Every instrument is present and the set is finished, and still nothing is answered — melancholia is the correct response to a taxonomy that is complete and insufficient at once.

## transformation

### trans introduction · `Trans_Introduction`

**`transform_composition`**

> *one after another is one. order matters*

One matrix holds every move, but only because a fourth coordinate was added to carry what three could not: the point's 1 against the direction's 0, a whole ontology smuggled in as bookkeeping.

### trans translation · `Trans_Translation`

**`transform_composition_workbench`**

> *compose: the hand builds the matrix*

To move is only to add, so the thing arrives as it left — but the void is not filled, only spanned, and the crossing is infrastructure that asks you to stand still and trust it.

### trans axisdecomposition · `Trans_AxisDecomposition`

**`toruscylinder`**

> *a ring and a tube: the same surface, one axis apart*

One move is three moves and the order does not matter — but only here, and the distance is not there at all until a body has walked it into being.

### trans rotation · `Trans_Rotation`

**`rotate_grid_cubes`**

> *the grid turns and stays a grid*

A turn needs something to turn around, and the moment it happens space stops being the same in all directions: rotation manufactures facing, and now order matters.

### trans rotationspectacle · `Trans_RotationSpectacle`

**`boolean_tunnel`**

> *a tunnel is a solid subtracted, turning*

Everything turns and the centre does not, and the long approach makes you pay for the arrival — the eye is the part that actually moved.

### trans scale · `Trans_Scale`

**`chair_assembly_puzzle`**

> *parts to chair: every piece a transform*

Scaling multiplies and adds nothing, so bigger is not more — and an object that asks to be scaled has been given a desire in order to make your hand feel invited.

### transformation · `Chamber_Transformation`

**`proximity_spawner`**

> *come close — something appears*

The catalyst does not damage the creature, it changes its state, and the whole argument of the chamber is that folded is not less: a transformation done to a body is contact, not harm.

### trans pit · `Trans_Pit`

**`pusher_block`**

> *pushed — translated by the room*

Here the transform is done to you, and the arithmetic that was neutral while it acted on objects is not neutral once the space it acts on is inhabited.
